#!/bin/bash --login

#SBATCH --job-name=eq_
#SBATCH --partition=Std-Long
#SBATCH --nodes=4
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=2
#SBATCH --time=24:00:00
#SBATCH --mail-type=ALL
#SBATCH --mail-user=user.name@domain.name
#SBATCH --error=./namd2.err.pbs
#SBATCH --output=./namd2.out.pbs

module load namd2

# SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR is the equivalent of PBS_O_WORKDIR
cd $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR

# Create a NAMD-compatible nodelist for charmrun from Slurm's environment
# This replaces the logic that used $PBS_NODEFILE
NODELIST="namd2.nodelist.${SLURM_JOB_ID}"
echo "group main" > $NODELIST
scontrol show hostnames $SLURM_JOB_NODELIST | while read host; do
  echo "host $host" >> $NODELIST
done

# Run the NAMD simulation using charmrun
# Note: $SLURM_NTASKS is used as the equivalent of PBS_NPROCS
charmrun `which namd2` +p$SLURM_NTASKS ++nodelist $NODELIST equilibrate_mobile.namd > solveq.log

issues: The filenames specified for `--error` and `--output` use a `.pbs` extension, which can be confusing as this is a Slurm script.
The script uses backticks for command substitution (`which namd2`). The more modern and recommended syntax is `$(which namd2)`.

inputs.script:
#!/bin/bash --login

#PBS -N eq_
#PBS -q Std-Long
#PBS -l nodes=4:ppn=2
#PBS -l walltime=24:00:00
#PBS -m abe
#PBS -M user.name@domain.name
#PBS -e ./namd2.err.pbs
#PBS -o ./namd2.out.pbs

module load namd2

cd $PBS_O_WORKDIR

NODES=`cat $PBS_NODEFILE`
NODELIST=$PBS_TMPDIR/namd2.nodelist
echo group main >! $NODELIST
for node in $NODES; 
  do
  echo host $node >> $NODELIST
done

charmrun `which namd2` +p$PBS_NPROCS ++nodelist $NODELIST equilibrate_mobile.namd > solveq.log
